items.title: Why Is Merck Stock Still Undervalued After An 80% Surge?
items.summary: You do not expect a pharmaceutical giant with a $376 billion market cap to put up numbers that make growth investors blush. Yet over the last 12 months, Merck (MRK) handed investors an 80% return, lapping the S&P 500. The apex occurred yesterday, August 19, 2026, when the stock surged to all-time highs.

items.title: The Key to Pharma M&A: Never Shopping Hungry
items.summary: Pharmaceutical chiefs are always hunting for drugs to replace expiring blockbusters. But shopping hungry can lead to expensive mistakes.

items.title: Is AbbVie Stock About To Break Out Again?
items.summary: AbbVie's upside case now turns on one pending dosing change for the medicine that supplies close to a third of guided revenue, and management expects it to speed up sales.

items.title: Cytokinetics Gains 20.5% YTD: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: Myqorzo's early launch momentum and global expansion could boost Cytokinetics, while pipeline progress may widen its growth opportunity.

items.title: Why Novartis, Lilly, and Bristol Myers Are Eyeing This Clinical-Stage Cancer Play
items.summary: A clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical startup with no product revenue just caught the attention of three of pharma's biggest acquirers, and the rights structure hiding inside its Lilly partnership may explain exactly why.

items.title: Bristol Myers Squibb to build $2.3B manufacturing campus in Houston
items.summary: The 600,000-square-foot campus will produce several types of medicines with room for expansion as digital integration and automation capabilities evolve.

items.title: 3 Absurdly Cheap Dividend Stocks to Buy for Under $100 Right Now
items.summary: Novo Nordisk, CVS Health, and Bristol Myers are top dividend stocks that are trading at modest valuations.

items.title: AstraZeneca scores in lung cancer; Sandoz inks a China deal
items.summary: A combination of AstraZeneca’s Tagrisso and Hutchmed’s Orpathys extended survival for some lung cancer patients. Elsewhere, MapLight floated the idea of partnering on its autism drug.
